notes: Pair extension tricks with content-type spoofing (Content-Type: image/jpeg) and magic-byte prefixing (GIF89a; or the raw \xFF\xD8\xFF JPEG header) when the filter also checks MIME/signature. Double extensions and trailing dots/semicolons exploit how Apache/IIS parse filenames. See the file-upload technique cards for full request examples. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 9 (Common Web Application Attacks).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Common Web Application Attacks

name: File Upload - Extension Bypass List
description: Alternate executable extensions to try when a file-upload filter blocks .php (or .asp). Blacklist filters often miss legacy or less-common handler extensions that the web server still executes. Switch tabs for PHP, ASP/ASPX, JSP and case/trick variants.

variations.label: ASP / ASPX
variations.description: Alternative web shell file extension for the target server technology. Each server-side language has specific extensions that the web server processes for code execution.

variations.label: JSP / other
variations.description: Alternative web shell file extension for the target server technology. Each server-side language has specific extensions that the web server processes for code execution.

variations.label: Trick variants
variations.command: shell.php.jpg   shell.php%00.jpg   shell.pHp   shell.php.   shell.php;.jpg   shell.php:.jpg
variations.description: File upload bypass technique using double extensions, null bytes, or alternative PHP extensions. Tricks the upload filter into accepting a PHP web shell as an image file.
